prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Researchers measured prefrontal cortex activity while participants either passively viewed emotional pictures or actively described them.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The participants with obesity performed 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling before being reassessed after a standardized recovery period.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Before the exercise, students with obesity reported lower positive feelings and showed reduced activity in the right orbitofrontal cortex while actively describing pictures.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: After the cycling session, the same students reported higher positive feelings and showed increased activity in the right orbitofrontal cortex during the active picture description task.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that because the study design lacked a control group, the observed changes cannot be definitively attributed to exercise, and further randomized trials are needed.
facts.subject: humans
